target: इस फ़ाइल को प्रिंट करने में दो मिनट लगे।
english: It took two minutes to print this file.
reason: UNNATURAL/officialese vocabulary — nobody says मुद्रक for a printer or दस्तावेज़ छापना in speech; both are literary/Sanskritized. Replacement keeps the 'X करने में N मिनट लगे' time-taken frame with the words people actually use (प्रिंट करना, फ़ाइल).

target: हमारे शहर में सर्दी दिसंबर में शुरू होती है।
english: In our city, winter starts in December.
reason: POINTLESS TRIVIA — Indian PIN codes are six digits everywhere, so 'our city's pin code is six digits' is a fact no one would ever state. Replacement keeps the same generic-habitual होता/होती है pattern and हमारे शहर vocabulary, but says something a learner really uses in small talk.

target: सरला ने सबको अपने घर खाने पर बुलाया।
english: Sarla invited everyone to her house for a meal.
reason: UNNATURAL register + vague situation — आमंत्रित करना is written/formal Hindi (speech uses बुलाना), and 'invited everyone in her village' is an odd, unusable scenario. Replacement keeps the same ने-perfective transitive structure with a real everyday invitation.

target: बचपन में हम गर्मियों में नानी के घर जाते थे।
english: As kids we used to go to grandma's house in the summers.
reason: NICHE + semantically wrong — threshing floors and bullocks are rural-historical trivia a learner will never use, and पीसना means 'grind', not 'thresh'. Replacement teaches the same habitual-past जाते थे pattern with a very common childhood-memory sentence.

target: रानी इस बारे में आपसे बात करना चाहती है।
english: Rani wants to talk to you about this.
reason: OFFICIALESE — 'इस विषय पर विस्तार से चर्चा करना' is meeting-minutes register, not spoken Hindi (and the very next card already teaches the natural version). Replacement keeps the infinitive + चाहती है structure in ordinary polite speech.

target: हमारी ट्रेन दो घंटे लेट चल रही है।
english: Our train is running two hours late.
reason: OFFICIALESE — प्रस्थान/विलंबित is station-announcement Sanskrit; a real person says 'ट्रेन लेट है/लेट चल रही है'. Replacement keeps the same delayed-train meaning in the register a learner needs to speak.

target: मैंने बोतल से पानी निकालकर गिलास में भरा।
english: I poured water out of the bottle and filled the glass.
reason: POINTLESS TRIVIA — an oilman and a bullock-driven oil press (तेली, कोल्हू) is vocabulary a learner will never need. Replacement keeps the identical 'X से निकालकर Y में भरा' conjunctive-participle frame with everyday objects.

target: मैंने अपने दोस्त को जन्मदिन पर एक किताब दी।
english: I gave my friend a book for his birthday.
reason: NICHE cultural trivia — disciple, guru and दक्षिणा (ritual offering) is not usable everyday content. Replacement keeps the same 'ने … को … दिया' giving/indirect-object pattern with ordinary vocabulary.

target: इस मौसम में सर्दी-ज़ुकाम आम है।
english: Colds are common in this season.
reason: TEXTBOOK/news-motto register — 'ups and downs in the stock market are normal' reads like a printed maxim, not speech, and सामान्य है is formal. Replacement keeps the same 'X में Y आम/सामान्य है' generalisation frame with content people actually mention.

target: स्कूल में झंडा फहराया गया और मिठाई बाँटी गई।
english: The flag was hoisted at school and sweets were distributed.
reason: UNNATURAL — 'सलामी दी और झंडा फहराया गया' mixes an active clause with no subject and a passive one, so it reads like a clipped report. Replacement keeps two coordinated passives (फहराया गया / बाँटी गई) in a setting learners actually encounter.
